description: One participant has no car and no public transport for the first part of the evening, so until 20:00 she can only reach what she can walk to — about a kilometre. The fairest venue is further than that, so the answer is a (venue, time) pair: the right place at the hour she can actually get to it, not the nearer place she can always reach.

candidateVenues.name: Herzl 16
candidateVenues.note: 80 m from Shira's door, so she can walk to it at any hour — but 6.76 km from Ben, whose burden of 0.845 is the worst any candidate imposes on anyone here.

candidateVenues.name: Bicicletta
candidateVenues.note: The fairest of the two and the better-rated — but 5.80 km from Shira, far beyond the kilometre she can walk before 20:00.

expected.reasoning: Straight-line burdens, all tolerances 8 km: Bicicletta is [0.725 Shira, 0.534 Liat, 0.131 Ben] and Herzl 16 is [0.845 Ben, 0.449 Liat, 0.010 Shira]. Leximin compares the worst-off participant first, so Bicicletta wins on 0.725 against 0.845 — and it is the better-rated venue too, so nothing pulls the other way and the only question left is the hour. Between 18:00 and 20:00 Shira has neither a car nor public transport, which leaves walking, and walking reaches about a kilometre (#89). Bicicletta is 5.80 km away, so every slot before 20:00 is invalid for her there; from 20:00 she has both back and it is comfortably inside her 8 km tolerance. The answer is therefore a (venue, time) pair, 20:00-23:00 — exactly three hours, the minimum a meeting may be. Two wrong answers this is designed to catch: Bicicletta at 18:00, which ignores the mobility window and proposes something Shira cannot reach, and Herzl 16, which over-reacts by dropping the venue rather than the hours and settles for the less fair option. Note the burden is a straight line with a detour correction, never a routed journey or a travel time (spec §5.4).
